analysis_refs.heading: Connected next: Book Dash
analysis_refs.text:
The public WordPress book type exposes source-native edition IDs and an explicit
language taxonomy. The catalog reported 1,116 language-edition entries and its
English taxonomy reported 214 when checked. A bounded **30-English-edition**
subset is now bundled and searchable alongside Gutenberg, textbooks and the
reviewed StoryWeaver set. This does not claim complete source coverage.

analysis_refs.heading: Owner clarification and actual access
analysis_refs.text:
Direct StoryWeaver requests returned HTTP 403 / browser-integrity error 1010.
A normal Chromium browser with the environment's proxy CA trust loaded the
public book pages, their metadata and the source's open-content policy. No
fingerprint spoofing, CAPTCHA handling, source login or credential replay was used.

analysis_refs.heading: Reviewed metadata
analysis_refs.text:
The [open-content policy](https://storyweaver.org.in/en/open-content) explicitly
covers all stories and illustrations under CC BY 4.0. Each reviewed item is a
book on that platform with its own metadata/credits and a linked policy; this
is not a claim about its readalong or video, which has different terms. The
terms link's browser shell was reachable, but its substantive terms content was
not independently verified. No comprehensive feed/API integration is claimed.

analysis_refs.heading: 8. Scale the integrations without scaling infrastructure prematurely
analysis_refs.text:
Refresh operational health and access evidence separately from long-term source
policy reviews. Use each source's documented limits/change cadence; monthly
directory gap reviews and periodic policy checks are planning defaults, not a
reason to hammer every endpoint daily. Suspend failing source actions honestly.
Current reading-evidence expiry rules remain in force unless explicitly revised
with evidence; source expansion does not renew stale StoryWeaver observations.

analysis_refs.heading: FCD01: contract decisions
analysis_refs.text:
- Content keys use `fcd:v1:<source>:<record>`; Gutenberg records are positive
  integer IDs; Europe PMC records include their source (`MED`, `PMC`, `PPR`).
  A DOI is an identifier, never an app key. Versions, translations, chapters and
  recordings retain distinct source-native keys. No fuzzy-title merge.
- Reviewed StoryWeaver translations use distinct native story IDs. The pilot
  requires English/Hindi/Tamil records with original credits, publisher levels
  and per-record review evidence before enablement.
- An omitted `kinds` searches books/learning resources. Paper searches supply
  paper kinds explicitly. Mixed book/paper requests are reported unsupported;
  the API never silently omits one requested scope.
- Search and resolve both accept `country` (ISO alpha-2 or absent/unknown) and
  language context. An observation for one explicit country does not establish
  availability in another. Gutenberg's US rights statement is retained with a
  generic country-rules prompt, not turned into a global legal claim.
- A reading action requires an explicit per-location `free_full_text` claim,
  positive evidence field/source/time, a safe supplied HTTP(S) URL, and an
  observation no older than 24 hours. Stale, missing, contradictory or
  country-mismatched observations become unknown; fetch failure is not absence.
  Reuse licence and free reading remain distinct. Missing licence never becomes
  an invented Creative Commons licence.
- `not_selected` means the planner did not query this source; `disabled` means
  it is not connected. `ok` with zero results is distinct from timeout,
  unavailable, throttled and quota-exhausted. Counts describe loaded items,
  never a federated global total.
- Default results contain anonymous free full text and a separately labelled verified free-account group (owner clarification 2026-11-01). An explicit unclear group may
  contain unknown/metadata-only items with labelled source links; previews,
  borrowing, unknown-price registration and restricted access stay excluded in v1.
- Source cursors remain server-owned. Browser tokens bind query, context,
  policy/index revisions and expiry. Shared live quota reservation and page
  advancement must pass a two-instance test before a live source is enabled.
  A memory implementation is a development/test adapter only; store failure
  disables uncapped live dispatch while keeping local metadata searchable.

analysis_refs.heading: FCD07-D: compare and repair the approved UI
analysis_refs.text:
537 server tests with real Redis/no skips, 141 client tests, 262 broad browser
journeys, 50 final feature journeys and 84 axe/overflow capture checks pass, with
typecheck/build/SEO/deployment. The actual Tamil StoryWeaver and Book Dash app
flows pass again through save/reload/reopen. Source data and hosted release gates
are unchanged. Consult the PR for CI at the current commit.

analysis_refs.heading: Actual sources and browser
analysis_refs.text:
Official Gutenberg/OTL/Book Dash refreshes retain all 1,000/1,909/30 native keys,
with zero semantic metadata changes. Current evidence supports 987/1,905/30
reading actions. These are bounded catalog counts, not global source totals.
The StoryWeaver reading-offer recheck failed; its previous observations are
retained, never renewed manually. #127 tracks that separate source-review gate.

analysis_refs.heading: Historical shared-store profile (superseded)
analysis_refs.text:
All flags default off. No hosted Redis service or production deployment has
been created by this implementation. Gutenberg, Open Textbook Library and Book Dash use
bundled metadata and require no database. The reviewed StoryWeaver set also
searches locally, including ordinary Free to read searches when its flag is on. Live paper sources need the shared
Redis REST URL/token and a strong random `CONTENT_CURSOR_SECRET` (at least 32
characters), plus an explicit daily/minute budget for each enabled source.
The build's `VITE_CONTENT_DISCOVERY_ENABLED` controls the Search scopes.

analysis_refs.heading: Reviewed source-account books
analysis_refs.text:
The three reviewed StoryWeaver books require `CONTENT_CHILDREN_ENABLED=true`
(and the normal discovery flag); the children's browse tile additionally uses
`VITE_CHILDREN_PILOT_ENABLED=true`. No source account or reader credentials are
stored by MyBookshelf. Source review/refresh instructions are in
[CHILDREN_REVIEW.md](CHILDREN_REVIEW.md). The refresh workflow checks these records
in a browser and refuses changed credits/levels, unknown charges or failed policy
checks. It proposes metadata; it never promotes production.

analysis_refs.heading: Enablement
analysis_refs.text:
Enable `CONTENT_DISCOVERY_ENABLED`, `CONTENT_CHILDREN_ENABLED`,
`VITE_CONTENT_DISCOVERY_ENABLED` and `VITE_CHILDREN_PILOT_ENABLED` for the checked
preview/production build, with separate strong server-only cursor signing secrets.
This publishes Gutenberg, Open Textbook Library, Book Dash and the reviewed
StoryWeaver set. Source-account requirements remain visible.

analysis_refs.heading: Evidence and limits
analysis_refs.text:
- The comparison fixtures are explicitly synthetic for papers/stories; they do
  not establish source access or represent the actual reviewed children's set.
  Their metadata is isolated in `client/e2e/free-content-ui-fixture.js`.
- The [actual-source app flows](evidence/2026-11-01/ui-review/actual-source-flow/expanded-sources-app-flow.json)
  separately exercise the real Tamil StoryWeaver record and Book Dash edition:
  search → detail → supplied source URL → save → reload → reopen, on desktop and
  phone, including 320px/200% text. Their credits and free-account condition are
  preserved. No source account was created and post-login reading is untested.
- Sources, counts, levels and available relations differ from the board samples.
  Only source-supplied versions/downloads/relations render; no v1/v2 list, recording,
  translation, cover art or licence is inferred to imitate sample data.
- The shared four-tab shell, desktop navigation rail and browser safe-area
  handling remain the existing app. The source sheet keeps its shared Close
  control. Catalog-subset disclosure and the owner-approved free-account group
  add necessary content beyond the original sample boards.
- Recent query history is bounded and lost on reload. It is not written to
  local storage, an account, analytics or a server history store.
- A fresh Europe PMC request on the current local API exceeded the five-second
  source deadline. The actual UI rendered an unavailable alert and no empty-copy
  claim. Earlier successful live-paper flows remain dated evidence, not a claim
  that the external service answered this later probe.
- The streamed-loading fixture uses the same local origin and `nosniff`/no-store
  headers as the app API. This avoids engine-dependent buffering/routing in the
  temporary review endpoint; it keeps the real progress assertions.
- Automated contrast/layout checks do not replace a screen-reader usability
  session. Firefox was not run locally. Remote CI covers WebKit as well.
- Hosted feature enablement, Redis-backed hosted paper journeys and the first
  scheduled refresh remain the previously recorded release gates. No flags,
  hosted credentials, storage or production deployment settings were changed.

analysis_refs.heading: Remaining release gates
analysis_refs.text:
- Hosted shared Redis REST binding and explicit per-source budgets; flags remain
  off without them. Local Gutenberg search requires no database.
- Reviewed real children’s metadata and local app journeys are now complete.
  The three StoryWeaver books require a free source account, as accepted by the
  owner; no source account was created and post-login reading was not tested.
- Automated reviewed catalog refresh before 24-hour access evidence expiry;
  the candidate tool/daily draft-PR workflow are now implemented and tested
  locally; first scheduled execution follows default-branch merge. Stale evidence
  remains unknown. No global Gutenberg/OTL completeness or deletion claim.
- Finish board-state coverage, source-specific retraction/version fixtures,
  fresh protected preview and final hosted release checks. WebKit runs in CI;
  Firefox is not part of the existing CI browser matrix and has not been run here.

analysis_refs.heading: Free source accounts and additional source delivery
analysis_refs.text:
The owner explicitly accepted free source login and assigned source research to
Codex. Public StoryWeaver metadata loaded in a normal browser even though direct
requests were blocked. Actual Read Story controls for records 7, 8 and 2252
returned 401 and a free signup offer. They are searchable as
`free_account_required`, grouped separately and labelled again before the source
reading link. Generic/unknown-price registration remains excluded. Explicit
`access: free_full_text` API requests remain anonymous-only. Old evidence becomes
unknown, and account-conditioned actions never invent direct file downloads.

analysis_refs.heading: Free source accounts and additional source delivery
analysis_refs.text:
Current real-source records: 1,000 Gutenberg, 1,909 textbook, 30 Book Dash and
three reviewed StoryWeaver records. This is 2,942 bounded metadata records,
not a worldwide catalog size or a search-match total. Eight sources have
implementations: these four book sources plus four existing live paper adapters.
The OpenAlex key was rechecked successfully. Redis remains deferred by the owner;
no hosted store, source account or production enablement was created here.

analysis_refs.heading: Phase C — children, regional and specialist coverage
analysis_refs.text: Reviewed children's pilot with approved metadata, attribution, language and level. Obtain feeds for comprehensive StoryWeaver/African Storybook/Book Dash search. Add CORE/HAL/Zenodo and India-specific providers in response to measured gaps; audio optional.

analysis_refs.heading: The ten candidates
analysis_refs.text:
This is ten discovery options, not ten demonstrated net-new origins in production.
GDL and BHL aggregate contributors; do not add their contributor counts on top.
BHL's Internet Archive hosting is not another source. Measure item/publisher
overlap with existing StoryWeaver, Book Dash, OTL and Gutenberg before reporting
incremental coverage. The five named publishers have distinct publisher IDs;
their chapters, editions and mirrored files do not increase that count.

analysis_refs.text: | GDL | English **Rain** page exposed 15 H5P chapter/page units; Hindi sample exposed 19, without login. Avoid double-counting StoryWeaver/other republished stories. |

analysis_refs.heading: C01. Children's books and early literacy
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval to investigate.** Prefer attributed coverage in an approved catalog,
an official export, or a supported publisher interface. An open-source website
codebase does not grant API access or metadata reuse. Free reader registration is
acceptable when disclosed; an advertised offer and verified post-login access are
separate observations. Recheck the existing StoryWeaver gate before expanding it.

analysis_refs.heading: Evidence boundaries and next handoff
analysis_refs.text:
Documentation opens succeeded for IBBY, Parag, Book Dash, Gutenberg, OTL, DOAB,
Project Madurai, LibriVox, DAISY and NLS during this planning review. The research
tool returned HTTP 402 for StoryWeaver's open-content page, 502 for NCERT's
textbook page and 403 for DPLA's API page. Sugamya redirected to its current domain
but exposed no readable content to the tool. These observations establish neither
payment requirements nor source-wide outages. No credentials, source accounts,
outreach, bulk harvests or live query qualification probes were performed.

analysis_refs.heading: Credentials and implementation inputs
analysis_refs.text: Assumptions: global discovery with explicit language/country context; lawful public hosts; verified free source login is allowed (owner clarification 2026-11-01), labelled separately from anonymous reading; no full-text hosting, subscription purchases, or library-card integration. Existing India library coverage makes NCERT, DIKSHA, StoryWeaver and Shodhganga useful follow-ups, but their discovery integrations are not assumed ready.

analysis_refs.heading: Current source work (2026-11-01)
analysis_refs.text:
The owner clarified that free source login is acceptable and asked Codex to
research additional sources. Three real StoryWeaver records in English, Hindi
and Tamil are now reviewed and searchable with an explicit free-account label;
no source account was created. Book Dash adds 30 real English-language editions
with public anonymous reading links. These are source-native metadata records,
not fictional board samples. The existing OpenAlex key was accepted by its API;
Redis setup is postponed, so live paper enablement remains deferred.
See [children’s review](CHILDREN_REVIEW.md), [additional sources](ADDITIONAL_SOURCES.md)
and [validation](VALIDATION.md). All source flags still default off pending the
intended hosted release checks; local metadata searches need no hosted store.

analysis_refs.heading: Behavior
analysis_refs.text:
Ten new integrations are released behind `CONTENT_KNOWLEDGE_ENABLED=true`:
Global Digital Library, LibriVox, Library of Congress digital books, Biodiversity
Heritage Library's Internet Archive collection, African Minds, LSE Press,
Mattering Press, mediastudies.press, punctum books and Python 3.15 documentation.
Five publisher catalogs share Thoth; this is not five separate API infrastructures.
The existing Gutenberg, Open Textbook Library, Book Dash and StoryWeaver snapshots
and the existing OpenAlex/Europe PMC integrations are also selectable. With the
existing production flags, this gives 16 connected sources, not 16 fully audited
origins or complete catalogs.

analysis_refs.heading: Verification and release record
analysis_refs.text:
The older snapshots had expired access observations. Their official metadata
exports/reading-gallery evidence were refreshed and audited: Gutenberg 1,000
records (unchanged identities), OTL 1,910 (+1, no removed IDs, one metadata edit),
Book Dash 30 pinned IDs (unchanged). No full books/art/audio were downloaded.
The existing 24-hour evidence rule still applies; future refresh proposals must
be reviewed/merged to keep these snapshot access labels current. StoryWeaver's
robots endpoint returned HTTP 403; its refresh stopped and the three historical
records remain available only with unclear access shown. It is not counted as a
current free-reading verification. No source account was created.

analysis_refs.heading: Production verification — 2026-11-05
analysis_refs.text: All ten new live query/detail samples and OpenAlex passed in production. Refreshed Gutenberg, OTL and Book Dash query/detail checks passed. StoryWeaver remains stale/unclear and is excluded by the default access filter. Two Europe PMC malaria probes timed out; the UI preserves that source error while other sources return results. This is an unresolved provider/runtime reliability observation, not a zero-result claim. The mobile WebKit all-source query completed all 16 groups with 26 loaded results, no page errors and no horizontal overflow; the LibriVox detail linked to the correct recording. See [saved production evidence](evidence/knowledge-release-2026-11-05/production/deployment.json), including failed probes and screenshots. The temporary preview share link was revoked after testing; protection settings were not weakened.
